To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate, in a rigorous fashion, that monocyte-derived DCs can efficiently cross-present melanoma Ags when co-culturing with a mixture of melanoma cells rendered Apo-Nec by γ-irradiation.
monocyte-derived DCs efficiently cross-present tumor antigens when cocultured with a mixed population of irradiated melanoma cells.

monocyte-derived dendritic cell (DC) can efficiently cross-presentation melanoma-associated Ag when co-cultures with a mixture of melanoma cells rendered by gamma irradiation apoptotic/necrotoic (Apo-Necto).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms involved in the cross-presentation of antigens by DCs, with special emphasis in tumor antigens.
the study of the interaction between dendritic cells and melanoma cells in the context of immunotherapy.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the cross-presentation of tumor antigens by human dendritic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of Apo-Nectic cells is a suitable source for native tumor antigens that provides maturation stimuli for DCs and allows efficient cross presentation of tumor associated antigens to T cells.
i) DCs can be loaded with a mixture containing Apo-Nec melanoma cells, ii) this loading is followed by DC maturation and iii) the cross-presentation of MelanA/MRT-1 and gp 100 Ags is efficient
Apo-Nec cell loaded DCs can be efficiently used for vaccination in melanoma patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new and efficient way to load dendritic cells with tumor antigens that can be used in the clinic for the treatment of cancer patients.
DCs loaded with a mixture Apo-Nec human melanoma cells efficiently present melanoma Ags to CD8+ T cells.
the use of apoptotic and/or necrotic melanoma-derived cells as a source of melanoma-associated Ag is an effective strategy for the induction of Ag cross-presentation and maturation of human DCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a mixture of four melanoma cell lines can be used to load DCs with native Ags and that the process is not limited to a particular Ag or HLA haplotype.
Apo-Nec cell-loaded DCs are a promising tool to generate potent CTL responses against human melanoma.
Apo-Nec cell mixtures can be used to cross-present tumor-associated Ags in vitro.
